title: Wallet Tools audit of the AUD-022 remediation, the self-tests of every tool and the MnemoCode and MHFE adoption, with remediation

reviewer.name: Claude Code coordinator and four scoped reviewers
reviewer.note: The coordinator ran as claude-opus-5-5 (the session's model identifier). The reviewers were subagents of that session; their model and reasoning effort were not recorded separately, and no effort setting was retained for any role.
roles: Coordinator: baseline runs, challenge of every candidate, remediation, final verification and report
selftests: startup and full self-tests of the four tools
mnemocode: MnemoCode adoption, recovery panels and parity with its command line
build: composition, provenance, release workflows and documentation

snapshot.workingTree: Dirty: nothing of the reviewed or remediated work is committed (owner's instruction of 2026-10-08: no commit and no push). HEAD alone does not identify the bytes; the source manifests below do.
snapshot.sourceFingerprintAlgorithm: SHA-256 of json.dumps(sorted path-to-SHA-256 map) of every tracked and untracked non-ignored path, excluding AUD-023-owned files (docs/audits/AUD-023-harnesses/capture-snapshot.py). Not the HTML build fingerprint.
snapshot.artifactRelationship: Both default editions built from the remediation tree by the recorded final-4-build (pnpm build) and accepted by final-4-artifact-profiles; the Linux launchers of both editions rebuilt (final-4-launchers-build, -dash) but not checked. The checks named final-3 ran on the final-3 tree, which differs from final-4 only in one count of tooling/verify-browser-regressions.mjs. dist/ is ignored and local.

upstream.state: Local commit, not on origin. All 134 vendored files are byte-equal with it (final-3-h-vendor-compare). The baseline reviewed c7a45234f4dac0935172fd0ede9d6c5d341524b2.

MHFE 0.5.1 browser package, a local build of a commit that is not pushed; manifest SHA-256 4f61ffb8...befd0. The baseline reviewed a build of d7af4b1035355a69779f8ad70a9dc50ba5b9ffd0 plus that repository's working tree.

procedureNote: docs/audit-report.schema.json was reformatted with Prettier at the owner's request during the audit (d47df012... to 989bf3de...); its content is unchanged. The other three files are byte-equal at baseline and at completion.

scope.method: Ordinary audit with a compact team (AGENTS.md): one coordinator and four reviewers with distinct scopes, not the expanded specialist workflow. The coordinator ran the baseline checks once on the reviewed tree and shared their logs; the reviewers wrote audit-only harnesses in docs/audits/AUD-023-harnesses/ and recorded every command they relied on. The coordinator challenged each candidate against the source before accepting it (21 accepted; several candidates were merged or kept as observations). The owner then authorised the remediation in the same working tree and decided four questions: a selective build offers MnemoCode's address check for its own coins only; two more release runners; JSON documents under format:check; MnemoCode's share-restore orchestration waits for its next round. During remediation MnemoCode 7dd510b648015a4d553b5be24ab2564f6edbb6b2 and MHFE 0.5.1 were vendored again, which brought Decode with marked codes, the heir-sheet known answers and MHFE's quick and full class checks into the Deriver. The final checks ran once on the remediation tree; harnesses whose expectations described the reviewed snapshot were adapted and say so in their files and READMEs. On 2026-10-08 the owner limited checks before a release to about two minutes each: the full unit suite, the build, the artifact checks, the Chromium browser regressions and the reviewers' probes ran; the Firefox regressions, selective builds and the launcher checks wait for the release and are listed as not run. Public test data only: 'abandon ... about', published vectors, the private key 1, synthetic lists.
included: The AUD-022 remediation (twenty findings) in the four tools and the Dash release workflow
Startup and full self-tests added to the Deriver, PSBT Inspector, Discovery Scanner and Activity Viewer, in both editions

MnemoCode adoption (c7a45234f4dac0935172fd0ede9d6c5d341524b2 at baseline, 7dd510b648015a4d553b5be24ab2564f6edbb6b2 at the end): recovery panels, workers, cards, shares, wallet recognition and parity with MnemoCode's command line

Build composition of selective Deriver builds, provenance and release gates, release workflows and documentation
excludedExecution: Reproducible container builds, canonical WASM rebuilds and launcher builds for other systems

Before the release, by the owner's instruction of 2026-10-08: the browser regressions in Firefox, the full recovery-backup-roundtrips case (real MHFE operations), the seven selective Deriver builds with their scan and startup, the thirteen self-test composition builds, and the launcher checks
MHFE's full-size vectors and any full-cost Argon2 run (minutes and 2 GiB each); MnemoCode's full vector replay
GitHub Actions runs (not authorised), so the release workflows are checked statically only
Live providers, real wallets and print acceptance of cards
scope.authorization: Review first (no product edits by reviewers), then remediation by the coordinator, authorised by the owner on 2026-10-07. No commit, push, tag or release (owner's instruction of 2026-10-08). MnemoCode and MHFE were not edited; requests went to their sessions.

environment.memory: About 15 GiB shared with the owner's programs; heavy commands ran one at a time under a lock, and the recorder stops a command's process group below 700 MiB available. No command was stopped for memory.

findings.title: Existing, typed or repaired shares cannot be printed or saved as a file (sskr-export outputs)
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Workspace rule: no utility is released while its browser package lacks a feature its command line has (precedent AUD-022-API003).
findings.reproduction: Repair shares in Forgotten › 'A code of a Shamir share'. No control prints them as cards or saves a share file; the card source says 'split the phrase into shares first'.
findings.expected: As sskr-export --output, --pdf, --cards-dir, --images-dir: the repaired shares saved one per line and printable as cards.
findings.observed: Card export took shares only from the last split; repair results offered Copy and QR per share only.
findings.impact: A parity gap of the browser package against the command line.
findings.recommendedFix: Let the card export and a share file take the shares a repair writes.
findings.requiredVerification: Repaired shares exported as a file and as cards in every layout.
findings.fix: RepairedShare.record and the outcome's one form (mnemocode-shares.ts); a share store for split and repaired shares (recovery-mnemocode-share-store.ts, origin split | repair); the repair result offers 'Save as a text file' and card printing; texts of the card source updated.
findings.verification: Unit test of the repaired-share record and form passes (final-unit). The coordinator's probe repairs a share in both editions, in Chromium and Firefox, saves the repaired shares as a text file (exactly the two shares, one per line) and prints them as cards at A6, A4 and business-card size (final-3-h-repaired-shares-2, 40/40; the first run, final-3-h-repaired-shares, expected the phrase cards' file names and is kept as a harness mistake).

findings.title: Selective Deriver builds carry other coins' self-test vectors and offer MnemoCode coins the build excludes
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Both canonical editions are correct; only selective builds are affected.
findings.reproduction: Build with --coins bitcoin: the page holds the Dash vectors XmN7PQYW…, 6PYMfcjo… and XbAei18d…, MnemoCode's EVM vector 0x9858EfFD… and 'Ethereum and EVM networks', runs the Dash vectors at startup and in the full self-test, and offers 11 MnemoCode coins; --coins ethereum offers none.
findings.expected: A build without a coin carries none of its checks or vector text (workspace rule); the owner chose (2026-10-07) that a selective build offers MnemoCode's address check for its own coins only, the other nine coins only in the full build.
findings.impact: Selective builds carry and run code of coins they leave out; the Ethereum-only build cannot recognise an Ethereum wallet.
findings.recommendedFix: Per-coin self-test modules composed by the build's coins; MnemoCode recognition chosen by the build's coins; per-coin markers in the gate.
findings.requiredVerification: The selective scan harness exits 0.
findings.fix: Part 1: per-coin signing and BIP38 self-test modules run through the functions the build composed (worker-runtime FeatureFunctions), composed per coin, with per-coin gate markers. Part 2 (owner's decision): a selective build offers and checks MnemoCode's addresses of its own coins only (mnemocode-offered-coins.ts in the full build, a generated list otherwise); a build without Bitcoin uses mnemocode-wallet-coins.ts; MnemoCode's coin checks are gated per coin (sharedSourceMarkers); the address-of-another-coin question is pruned from builds that offer none.
findings.verification: Unit tests of the composition, the per-coin checks and the offered coins pass (final-unit). Not run: the selective scan of seven variant builds, its required verification; it waits for the release (owner's instruction of 2026-10-08: checks longer than about two minutes only before a release).
findings.remainingRisk: MnemoCode's core/wallet-evidence.ts imports core/coins.ts, so a selective build with Bitcoin still bundles the code of every coin family (not their known answers, and none of them is offered). MnemoCode was asked to let the host pass its coins (message of 2026-10-08).

findings.title: BIP85 and Silent Payments derive after the startup self-test failed
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The workspace rule and the README promise that a failed startup check keeps the feature's controls closed; the new BIP85 and BIP352 checks were switched off by this gap.
findings.reproduction: Change the BIP85 WIF expected literal of a copy of the dist Deriver by one character (CSP hash recomputed). The badge reads 'Cryptographic self-test failed: BIP85 WIF.' Type 'abandon … about', tick Child seeds (BIP85) and open its tab: a 12-word child phrase appears; tick Silent Payments: an sp1q… address appears.
findings.expected: Both tabs stay closed, as the main derivation, search and generation do.
findings.observed: bip85-feature.ts derive/scheduleRefresh and silent-payment-feature.ts derive never consulted the self-test verdict; view.setCryptoControlsEnabled covered only derive, search and generate.
findings.impact: A build whose BIP85 or BIP352 known answers came out wrong still handed out child phrases and receiving addresses. A wallet funded from a wrong BIP85 child cannot be derived again elsewhere. A red badge and an error line were shown; nothing left the page.
findings.recommendedFix: One gate for every control that derives, signs or encrypts from the phrase; a failed full self-test closes them as a failed startup does.
findings.requiredVerification: Unit tests that no worker request is made before the self-tests pass; a browser case with an injected startup failure in both editions and engines.
findings.fix: crypto-self-test-gate.ts (SELF_TEST_NOT_PASSED); cryptoReady in bip85-feature (with setEnabled), silent-payment-feature (with setEnabled), the child wallet's Silent Payments, message-signing-feature and bip38-encryption-feature; controller.failCryptoSelfTest for a failed startup or full self-test (onFullSelfTestFailure); FullSelfTestSection.onFailure.
findings.verification: Unit tests (final-unit: bip85-feature, bip85-child-silent-payment, controller, full-self-test) pass; browser case self-test-failure passes in the Chromium browser regressions of both editions (final-3-browser-regressions-chromium-multi-chain, -dash-community); the reviewer's reproduction passes, adapted to the fail-closed full self-test (final-3-h-selftests-browser-3, 59/59). The Firefox regressions wait for the release.

findings.title: A card export that finishes late puts back QR images of an old phrase or a replaced share set
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Same class as AUD-022-SEC001/SEC002: recovery material that the page removed comes back after the change that removed it.
findings.reproduction: Seedshift 23-09-2026, Colors, A6, 'Add one QR code', PNG. Press Save cards and type another phrase while it renders; or split 2-of-3, print the shares and press Split again while they render.
findings.expected: No QR image of the old phrase or the replaced shares after the change, and no file of them.
findings.observed: forgetQrImages ran on the change, then the export finished and called qrImages.replaceChildren(...) with the old payloads; the status described the old set.
findings.impact: Recovery material shown again and savable as PNG after it was removed; an obsolete share set could be mixed up with the new one. Nothing left the page.
findings.recommendedFix: A revision moved by every change that removes the QR images; a late export drops its file, images and status.
findings.requiredVerification: Both probes pass with a normal export as control; a browser regression case.
findings.fix: exportRevision in recovery-mnemocode-cards.ts; a stale export wipes its bytes, saves nothing and says so (STALE_EXPORT). LinkedSources now announces an expired link, so a phrase linked from Generate & Derive that changes or is cleared also removes what the panel made from it.
findings.verification: Browser case mnemocode-late-cards passes in the Chromium browser regressions of both editions (final-3-browser-regressions-chromium-multi-chain, -dash-community); the reviewer's probes late-card-qr and late-card-qr-shares pass, adapted to the export that now saves nothing (final-3-h-mnemocode-browser-2, 9 probes, none failed).

findings.title: The Dash-only recognition accepts any address count and addresses on a fingerprint
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The page checked the count first; the library refused it at the first candidate.
findings.reproduction: DashRecognition.assertEvidence accepts counts 0, -1, 1.5, 1001, 2^53, NaN, Infinity and "20"; MnemoCodeSearches.words then throws at the first candidate.
findings.expected: Refused before any work, as the Bitcoin edition does, with MnemoCode's own comparison.
findings.observed: mnemocode-wallet-dash.ts re-implemented part of CoinAddressComparison and skipped addressCount.
findings.impact: A late refusal with a less clear message; no wrong match.
findings.recommendedFix: Build MnemoCode's CoinAddressComparison in assertEvidence and refuse addresses on a fingerprint.
findings.requiredVerification: The harness case passes for the Dash edition.
findings.fix: mnemocode-wallet-coins.ts replaces mnemocode-wallet-dash.ts and mnemocode-wallet-fingerprint.ts: assertEvidence builds MnemoCode's CoinAddressComparison (address, place and count) for an offered coin and refuses a count beside a fingerprint.
findings.verification: The reviewer's harness, adapted to the new module, passes with the Dash edition's bad counts refused (final-3-h-coin-evidence, 21/21); the unit test passes (final-unit).

findings.title: Command-line options without a browser field: Bitcoin profile list, collection title, sample card outputs

findings.expected: The same choices in the page.
findings.impact: Parity gaps; samples silently ignored two chosen settings.
findings.recommendedFix: Checkboxes for the address types, a collection title field, samples in every output of preview.
findings.requiredVerification: Unit test of the sample outputs; the coin-evidence and cards browser cases.
findings.fix: Address types as checkboxes in three places (none ticked: every type); #mnemocode-card-title for phrase cards and samples, hidden for shares as the share commands refuse --title; renderSamples returns a card file in PDF, PNG/JPEG (one image or a ZIP) or separate cards, with QR and title.
findings.verification: Unit test in mnemocode-cards.test.ts passes (final-unit); browser cases mnemocode-cards and mnemocode-coin-evidence pass in the Chromium browser regressions of both editions (final-3-browser-regressions-chromium-multi-chain, -dash-community).

findings.title: Regression tests for AUD-022-API004, API007 and API003 do not reach the reproduced path

findings.impact: A future regression of these fixes would pass CI.

findings.requiredVerification: The new tests pass and fail with the two mutations.

findings.title: MnemoCode logic is copied instead of bound
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Every rule is MnemoCode's and the outputs match; the risk is divergence.
findings.reproduction: mnemocode-shares.ts (595 lines) re-creates the step order of the CLI's restorePhrases and sskr-export; the page copied addressCount with its own message and default; parseMnemoCodeDates repeated DatesAnswer.parse's splitting without its limits.
findings.expected: The page only translates input and output (workspace rule).
findings.impact: Rules can drift apart between the CLI and the page.
findings.recommendedFix: Upstream exposes the restore/export flow as a core class; the page calls addressCount/defaultAddressCount and DatesAnswer.
findings.requiredVerification: The copies are gone.
findings.fix: Local parts fixed: the page uses MnemoCode's addressCount/defaultAddressCount and DatesAnswer, and MAX_SHOWN_CANDIDATES/MAX_SHOWN_MATCHES instead of copies. The restore/export orchestration stays until MnemoCode's ShareRestore (agreed with MnemoCode for its next round; deferred by the owner).
findings.verification: Local parts fixed and covered by the unit suite (final-unit). Deferred by the owner: the share restore and export orchestration stays a copy until MnemoCode's ShareRestore class exists (asked for its next round).
findings.remainingRisk: A change in MnemoCode's share restore must be copied by hand until then; the vendor comparison and the share tests catch byte or behaviour drift, not a missed rule.

findings.title: Builds without SSKR carry and run MnemoCode's share-card self-test and renderer
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No wrong output; dead code and a check of an absent feature.
findings.reproduction: Builds kd-no-sskr and kd-dash-community-no-sskr list 'MnemoCode share card known answers' at startup and hold ur:sskr/gogrrsbyadadbn… and '4BBF-1-1 4BBF-1-2'.
findings.expected: Only a host that offers share cards adds the test (MnemoCode's own comment).
findings.impact: Bundle size and a check of an absent feature.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the test and the renderer only with mnemocode-cards and sskr, with a marker.
findings.requiredVerification: The kd-no-sskr builds hold none of it.
findings.fix: Share-card checks and renderer behind swap modules (mnemocode-share-card-checks.ts, mnemocode-share-render.ts, each with a -none twin) chosen by the sskr feature; the startup check renamed self-test-mnemocode-share-cards.ts and composed with mnemocode-cards and sskr; a shared marker set.
findings.verification: The composition gates refuse the share-card modules without SSKR, and their unit tests pass (final-unit: selective-composition). Not run: the selective builds without SSKR and their scan, which wait for the release.

findings.title: The vendored MHFE runtime WASM embeds the builder's home-directory paths, and no gate looks inside WASM
findings.releaseBlockingReason: CI already refuses this unreleased MHFE pin, so it cannot ship.
findings.reproduction: strings packages/recovery-mhfe-wasm/generated/runtime/mhfe.wasm | grep -c /home/ gives 21 panic locations under the builder's cargo registry; both Derivers embed it as base64.
findings.expected: No absolute builder path in any shipped module; the released v0.5.0 WASM and this project's four modules hold none.
findings.observed: As described; the HTML gates scan text only and base64 hides the strings.
findings.impact: Names the builder's account and makes bytes differ between machines.
findings.recommendedFix: Vendor a path-remapped MHFE build; a gate that decodes embedded WASM and refuses absolute paths.
findings.requiredVerification: The gate refuses the current package and passes a remapped one.
findings.fix: tooling/builder-paths.mjs: assertNoBuilderPaths in verify-wasm-producers (every generated module and MHFE's) and assertEmbeddedWasmWithoutBuilderPaths over every finished page in verify-artifact-profiles. MHFE remaps the paths in its build (its AUD-010).
findings.verification: tooling/builder-paths.test.mjs passes (final-unit); pnpm build passes the gate with MHFE 0.5.1 (final-3-build); the reviewer's harness finds no builder path (final-3-h-wasm-paths).

findings.title: Two of the five published executables are never started before publication
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The comments and RELEASING.md overstated what ran; the owner chose to add the two runners.
findings.reproduction: The launcher jobs run on ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025 and macos-15 (arm64); the verifier starts only the host's platform, so linux-aarch64 and macos-x86_64 are published unstarted, while the comments say every executable is started on its own system.
findings.expected: Every published executable started before publication, or an accurate statement.
findings.impact: An executable nobody ran could be published.
findings.recommendedFix: Add ARM Linux and Intel macOS runners, or correct the texts (owner chose the runners).
findings.requiredVerification: Static workflow review; the next release run.
findings.fix: ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-15-intel added to the launcher matrix of both release workflows; comments, launchers.yml header and RELEASING.md say which systems start which executable.
findings.verification: Static check of both workflows passes (final-3-h-release-workflows). Not run: the workflows themselves (GitHub Actions runs are not authorised), so no executable was started on the two new runners.

findings.title: The new release gates have no test that makes them refuse
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The gates work (build-provenance-ci-refusal shows it); only their refusal tests were missing.
findings.reproduction: Every test stubs CI to empty and passes verifyFixedSources: false; no test triggers assertReleasedUpstreams under CI=true or verifyMhfePackage on a changed, missing or extra file.
findings.expected: A verifier is also given a case it must refuse.
findings.impact: A regression that disabled either gate would pass the tests.
findings.recommendedFix: Tests that make both gates refuse.
findings.requiredVerification: The new tests pass and fail with the gate removed.
findings.fix: assertReleasedUpstreams(logger, sources, ci) and verifyMhfePackage(root, pin) exported; tests for CI refusal, a local warning, and a changed, extra and missing MHFE file and a changed manifest.
findings.verification: Refusal tests pass (final-unit: verify-dependency-provenance.test.mjs); the reviewer's harness passes (final-3-h-provenance-ci-refusal).

findings.title: Five adoption files are missing from the MnemoCode provenance list
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The record lacked hashes of first-party integration files; no integrity check was bypassed.
findings.reproduction: recovery-mnemocode-share-handover.ts, recovery-mnemocode-worker-job.ts, self-test-mnemocode-cards.ts, tests/mnemocode-search.test.ts and recovery-mnemocode-backup-check.test.ts were not in the mnemocode-codec list; no test checked the list.
findings.expected: Every file that binds MnemoCode is recorded.
findings.impact: The provenance record could omit integration files.

findings.requiredVerification: The list holds every file of the naming convention.

findings.verification: The completeness test of the dynamic provenance list passes (final-unit).

findings.title: The public-input guard's startup check is missing where the guard is used
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A documented security claim of both shipped Discovery editions was false.
findings.reproduction: grep -c 'Public-input guard refuses' gives 0 in both dist Discovery artifacts; a Viewer built with --coins bitcoin calls the guard but never tests it.
findings.expected: The guard's known answers run wherever the guard screens inputs (Discovery README).
findings.observed: Only the watch-only-only Discovery build ran it.
findings.impact: A broken guard would go unnoticed at startup in the default Discovery builds and in Viewers without Dash.
findings.recommendedFix: Run the guard's check wherever it is built; an artifact marker; the regression asserts it.
findings.requiredVerification: The marker in both Discovery artifacts and the self-tests regression lines.
findings.fix: discovery-composition adds public-input-self-test.ts to seed builds with watch-only discovery; external-activity runs the guard's check before its address checks; the Discovery artifact verifier requires the marker; the self-tests case asserts both lines.
findings.verification: Default builds: the Scanner artifact verifier requires the guard line (final-4-artifact-profiles) and the self-tests browser case asserts it in the Chromium browser regressions of both editions (final-3-browser-regressions-chromium-multi-chain, -dash-community). A Viewer built with Bitcoin only carries the guard check (final-4-viewer-bitcoin-build, final-4-viewer-bitcoin-guard), through the same startup path (external-activity.ts) that the self-tests case runs in the default Viewer.

findings.title: The max-results field limits word searches to 100 where recover-word shows every candidate
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The table said how many were hidden and the field could be raised.

findings.title: The Scanner's candidate-list controls stay open after a failed startup self-test
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Scanning stays blocked, so candidates are never scanned or sent.

findings.requiredVerification: A unit test of the closed panel and of close() after a failure.

findings.verification: candidate-list-panel.test.ts passes (final-unit); the reviewer's reproduction, which no longer clicks a closed button, passes (final-3-h-selftests-scanner-gate-2).

limitations: Nothing is committed: fix and verification commits do not exist, and the statuses bind to the remediation source fingerprint instead.
MnemoCode 16ccca1 and MHFE 0.5.1 are unreleased local builds; the provenance gate refuses a release with them by design, and a final re-vendor of their published releases needs a delta review.
No full-cost Argon2, MHFE full-size vectors or MnemoCode vector replay; MHFE's quick and full class checks ran in the browser regressions only.
The release workflows were checked statically; no GitHub Actions run, so no executable started on any runner, including the two added ones.

Not run on the remediation tree, waiting for the release by the owner's instruction (checks of more than about two minutes only before a release): the browser regressions in Firefox, the whole recovery-backup-roundtrips case, the selective builds (seven variants with scan and startup, thirteen composition builds) and the launcher checks. At the reviewed snapshot the selective builds ran; their results are in the review records.

The Chromium regressions of both editions ran on the final-3 tree: every case passed except recovery-backup-roundtrips, which stopped at its first step because Decode's new question for codes marked ? adds a help popover (27, not 26). The remediation corrected that count in tooling/verify-browser-regressions.mjs (the only difference between the final-3 and final-4 trees), and coordinator-help-count.mjs confirms 27 in both built pages; the rest of the case waits for the release.
The node:vm control-flow probes of the remediation reviewer are bound to the baseline bytes and were not rerun on changed files; the repository's own tests stand for them there.
Reviewer harnesses whose expectations described the reviewed snapshot were adapted after remediation (each says so); their baseline records stay as they were.
Unit counts of overlapping runs are not added; interim development runs during remediation were not recorded and are not counted.
This is a targeted security-sensitive review with tests, not a certification that no defect remains.

assessment.releaseAcceptedReason: Nothing is committed, MnemoCode and MHFE are vendored from unreleased local builds (the provenance gate refuses a release with them), and the open items below remain.
assessment.verificationLevel: Security-sensitive targeted execution on the remediation tree: the full unit suite, both default builds and their artifact checks, the Chromium browser regressions of both editions and the reviewers' probes, each within about two minutes. Not release-level: the Firefox regressions, selective builds, launcher checks, reproducible container build, vector replays and full-cost Argon2 wait for the release.
assessment.summary: The reviewed tree had no critical or high finding. Two medium findings let a page keep working after its known answers failed (AUD-023-SEC001) or show recovery material that had been removed (AUD-023-SEC002); both are fixed and their browser cases pass in the Chromium regressions of both editions. The AUD-022 remediation held: 16 of its 20 findings are verified, and the four left as fixed need a workflow run or a full-cost MHFE rekey that this audit did not perform. On the remediation tree the full unit suite, both default builds and their artifact checks, the Chromium browser regressions and the reviewers' reproductions pass; the larger checks listed below wait for the release, and the findings that depend on them stay fixed rather than verified.
